question:
Choose the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

__**Figurative **__language employs words with meanings not strictly literal, but varying from their ordinary definitions.
solution:
The correct answer is**: Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"figurative"** means using figures of speech; symbolic,** not literal**. (रूपकात्मक)

 
 
• **Example: **She used **figurative** language to describe the storm as a fierce lion.
 
 
 
• **"Literal" **refers to taking words in their usual or most basic sense without metaphor or allegory. (शाब्दिक)
 
 
• **Example: **When he said he could eat a horse, he didn't mean it in a** literal** sense.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'figurative' **is **'literal'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Descriptive **(वर्णनात्मक): Serving or seeking to describe.

 
 
• **Example:** The descriptive passage vividly painted a picture of the bustling marketplace.
 
 
 
• **Fanciful **(कल्पनाप्रधान): Over-imaginative and unrealistic.
 
 
• **Example: **His fanciful ideas about the future often seemed unrealistic to others.
 
 
 
• **Flowery** (सजावटी): Full of elaborate or literary words and phrases.
 
 
• **Example:** The poet's flowery language made the poem beautiful but hard to understand.
 
 

 

32:Tb9f,

The correct answer is: **Option 2.**
